Date: 2026-11-10. Five seats opened (high-risk).

cells.title: Project the Claude settings baseline add-only in onboarding
cells.action: Keep contract 282a650f. In onboard/hooks_wiring.rs widen the worktree-tool projection into the Claude settings baseline of decision bd6ebab1: one constant set (allow EnterWorktree, ExitWorktree; deny EnterPlanMode, ExitPlanMode, DesignSync, NotebookEdit, SendMessage, PushNotification, RemoteTrigger, ReportFindings, ScheduleWakeup, AskUserQuestion, CronCreate, CronDelete, CronList; permissions.defaultMode bypassPermissions; top-level disableBundledSkills, disableWorkflows, disableRemoteControl, disableClaudeAiConnectors, disableArtifact true and syncClaudeAiSkills false). Replace worktree_tool_allow_missing and merge_worktree_tool_allow with claude_settings_missing(repo_root, full) and merge_claude_settings(path, full); full=false owns only the two allow names, exactly today's behavior. Add-only: append missing allow/deny names after existing entries in baseline order; write defaultMode only when permissions has none; write a top-level key only when absent; keep every other key, entry and order; a parse failure, non-object top level, non-object permissions or non-array allow/deny returns the text unchanged. Rename the plan item to merge_claude_settings in plan.rs and its apply arm in apply.rs (apply re-checks before writing). Add the --no-claude-settings onboard flag (bool, default off) in mod.rs and the registry, and a project preference read exactly like statusline_config_preference (.bee/config.json "claude_settings": false, never written by onboarding); full is false when the flag is given OR the preference is false (D5). claude_settings_missing returns false for every shape the merge refuses, and deny, defaultMode and the switches are inspected only when full is true. In notices.rs add claude_settings_notices, emitted in plan and apply output whenever merge_claude_settings with full=true is listed: one 'notice: ' line saying Claude permission prompts are turned off for this project and the baseline tools are denied, naming each baseline key kept at the project's own value and each baseline deny name the project's allow list already carried, saying the baseline is written even when bee's guard hooks are not wired, and naming --no-claude-settings and "claude_settings": false as the opt-outs (D6, D7); bump any pinned flag count (catalog.rs PINNED_FLAG_COUNT, reservations/flags.rs, cli_shape.rs) with the new flag. Red first: keep the assertions of the four hooks_wiring.rs worktree tests (hooks_wiring.rs:1422, :1444, :1474, :1492) under full=false, renamed, and update the six onboard/tests.rs end-to-end tests at :2827-:2929 that pin the item name merge_worktree_tool_allow; and add tests: a fresh file gets the whole baseline; a file with defaultMode default and an allow list keeps both and gains the rest; deny entries are appended once; a second merge is unchanged; --no-claude-settings on a fresh repo writes only the two allow names; an onboard apply then a plan reports up_to_date; an already-onboarded host shape (the two allow names, hooks and statusLine present, no deny, no defaultMode) gains the baseline, keeps every hooks and statusLine key in order, and takes one .bak; a non-array deny plans nothing and reports up_to_date; "claude_settings": false with a bare apply writes no defaultMode, deny or switch; the notice names a kept defaultMode and an allowed-then-denied tool. Knowledge delta in the same commit: in docs/knowledge/areas/onboarding/host-project-artifacts.md widen the worktree-tool paragraph to the baseline and its opt-out, citing this feature's CONTEXT.md D1-D3 (not raw decision ids), with a Read when: line if the concept lacks one. No code comments. One commit.
cells.verify: cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p bee -- claude_settings onboard

truths: Onboarding a repo with no .claude/settings.json writes the whole baseline
A present permissions.defaultMode, a present top-level key and existing allow/deny entries are never changed or reordered
Missing allow and deny names are appended once; a second apply plans nothing
The --no-claude-settings flag writes only EnterWorktree and ExitWorktree, as before
An unparsable or odd-shaped settings file is left unchanged
An opted-out host (flag or config preference) gets no baseline on a later bare apply
Onboarding prints a notice whenever it plans or writes the full baseline, naming kept keys and the opt-outs
An already-onboarded host gains the baseline with its hooks and statusLine untouched

artifacts.substantive: the baseline constant set, claude_settings_missing and merge_claude_settings with tests

key_links: plan.rs plans merge_claude_settings only when claude_settings_missing; apply.rs re-checks before writing
open_choices: Whether full=false is a separate constant or a filter over the baseline

cells.title: Pass --no-claude-settings through both installers
cells.action: Mirror --no-statusline exactly. scripts/install.sh: add --no-claude-settings to the usage text (one entry saying it skips the Claude settings baseline — bypass mode, the denied tools and the six switches — and keeps the worktree-tool allow), to the argument parser, and to the ONBOARD_FLAGS pass-through; add one Safety bullet saying the baseline is add-only and never overwrites a present value, that an already-onboarded project gains it on its next install or onboard apply, that it is written even with --no-hooks, and that "claude_settings": false in .bee/config.json opts out for good. scripts/install.ps1: add the matching -NoClaudeSettings switch, its help line, and the '--no-claude-settings' pass-through into $onboardFlags. Prove with bash -n scripts/install.sh, a pwsh parse check of install.ps1 when pwsh exists (name it skipped otherwise), and rg showing the flag in both scripts. Then run .bee/bin/bee dev regen so the release manifest records the new installer bytes, and commit the manifest with the scripts. One commit.

truths: install.sh names --no-claude-settings in its help and passes it to onboarding
install.ps1 accepts -NoClaudeSettings and passes --no-claude-settings to onboarding
install.sh's Safety section says the baseline is add-only

artifacts.substantive: flag in usage, parser and ONBOARD_FLAGS

key_links: both installers reach the same onboarding flag
prohibitions: No settings edit in shell or PowerShell code

cells.title: Consolidate this feature's knowledge and write its delivery
cells.action: Run the writer consolidation step on this feature: run `bee knowledge consolidate --feature claude-settings-baseline`. Dedupe and trim the deltas the cells wrote, anchor each concept to the code it describes, never restate code, and write docs/history/claude-settings-baseline/delivery.md listing the concepts changed and why, one line each. Cite this feature's CONTEXT.md D-numbers, never raw decision ids, and state in one sentence that denying AskUserQuestion makes gate questions plain chat text in hosts, and route every D-ID (D1-D7) into a docs/knowledge concept. Run `.bee/bin/bee knowledge check` green. One commit.

truths: the onboarding concept states the baseline, add-only rules and opt-out, anchored to code
delivery.md lists each concept changed with one line on why
prohibitions: No raw decision ids in docs outside docs/history/claude-settings-baseline/
